Nos.: 9250361 / 9207783 / 9250347 (Fax) Direct Lines: 925-0:3-40; 925-03-3,3 Fax No.: 925-03-41 nn t OPINION NO. 23 OFFICE OF THE SECRETARY March 15, 2005 MAYOR CESAR C. SULIBIT Lifiw, Laguna Dear Mayor Sulibit: s. 200&_ This pertains to your letter seeking our legal opinion on the following quoted queries, Io wit: 1. Whether or not the Punong Barangay who went out of the country can still collect his honorarium. 2. Whether there is a prescriptive period on the said absence. (He filed a six (6) months vacation leave) 3. Who will assume the posüion of the Punong Barangay on the span of time he is having his vacation. 4. What is the status of the leave of the Punong barangay if he sent his Application for Leave two (2) days after his departure. 5. Whether or not the designation as Officer in Charge of the 4th Kagawad of the Sangguniang Barangay by the Punong Bayan is valid. In reply to your first query, please be informed that barangay officials are compensated in the form of honoraria pursuant fo the Department of Budget and Management Local Budget Circular No. 63 dated October 22, 1996. In

-2 relation to the said DBM Circular, Section 288 of the Government Accounting and Auditing Manual also provides that services must be rendered before a public official shal be entitled to receive the honorarium appurtenant thereto. In view thereof, the punong barangay who travels abroad cannot collect/claim his honorarium because there is here the absence of the required actual services rendered. In reply to your second query, may we invite your attention to Section 81 3d par. of the Local Government Code of 1991 which provides that "Elective local officials shall be entitled to the same leave privileges as those enjoyed by appointive local officials, including the commulation and commutation thereof. Corollary thereto, Section 5 of CSC Memo Circular No. 41 s. 1998 also provides that "xxx local elective officials shall be entitled to leave privileges as those enjoyed by appointive local officials xxx". In this regard, Section 57 of the 'Leave without pay not above mentioned circular also provides that: exceeding one year may be granted, in addition to the vacation and or sick leave earned. Leave without pay in excess of one month shall require the clearance of the proper head of department or agency." Ergo, we are of the view that a leave of absence for one year may be availed of by the concerned Punong Barangay. With regard to your 3rd and 5th query, Section 46(a) of the Local Government Code of 1991 provides for the rule on who has the right to assume office in case of temporary vacancy in the Office of the Punong Barangay. It states that:. "SECTION 46(a) — When the governor, city or municipal mayor or punong barangay is temporarily incapacitated to perform his duties for physical or legal reasons such as, but not limited to, leave of absence, travel abroad, and suspension from office, the vice governor, city or municipal vice-mayor or the highest ranking sanqguniang barangay member shall automatically exercise the powers and perform the duties and functions of the local chief executive concerned, except the power to appoint, suspend, or dismiss employees which can only be exercised if the period of temporary incapacity exceeds thirty (30) working days. Under this premise, it is clear that the highest ranking sangguniang barangay member shall automatically assume the office of the punong

barangay in case of the latter's absence or travel abroad. Thus, the designation of the 4th ranking sanggunian barangay member as Acting Punong Barangay by the Punong Bayan is therefore bereft of any legal basis. Anent your 4th query, may we, at the outset, restate Section 41 of CSC Memorandum Circular No. 41 , s. 1998, thus: "SECTION 41 — All application for vacation leave of absence for one (1) full day or more shall be submitted on the prescribed form for action by the proper head of agency five (5) days in advance, whenever possible, of the effective dote of such leave.' Based on the above cited provision, it is clear that the application for vacation leave shall be submitted five days in advance. However, as to its effect, we suggest to address this query with the Civil Service Commission, the central personnel agency of the government. Furthermore, we would also like to stress that an elective tocal officials who will travel abroad, official or unofficial, must secure travel authority from the Secretary of Department of Interior and Local Government pursuant to DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2001-52, dated May 8, 2001 Hope we have enlightened you on the matter. cc: Dir. Leonilo B. Lariosa DILG Region IV-A CALABARZON 827 Calderon BFdg., EDSA, Quezon Ci'y 100 Very truly yours, ANGELO T. REY S OF EmoR REPLYING. SILG05-005053
